A 3DV-190 and two CV-190 units

The setup on site included a 3DV-190 and two CV-190 units. We could receive a combined left/right image from the 3DV-190, or capture each view separately from the two CV-190 units.

A3DV-190
We captured both views, combined as SBS, from a single output.
B · CCV-190 ×2
We captured the DVI-D output from each unit as the left and right inputs on the Mac.

One SBS input or two separate views

On April 22, we used one capture card for the SBS output from the 3DV-190. On October 29, we connected the DVI outputs from the two CV-190 units to separate capture cards. The Mac input configuration depends on whether the incoming video already contains both views.

Combining the views
Handled by the Mac app

Connecting two DVI outputs to the Mac

For dual capture, each DVI-D output was converted to HDMI, then connected to the Mac through the capture card’s USB output. Each view needs its own adapter and capture card.

In the Mac app, we assigned one capture device to the left input and the other to the right. The Mac synchronizes the incoming frames and combines them into SBS.

Combining two inputs into an SBS frame

Each capture input carries one view. The Mac places the two views in the left and right halves of a single side-by-side (SBS) frame.

After receiving the frame, the Galaxy XR app displays the left region to the left eye and the right region to the right eye.
